result.rationale: In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts the diff literally defines `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. Zod schemas are plain objects with no custom toString, so both computed keys evaluate to "[object Object]", and z.object strips unknown keys — the intended expiry capture never happens. The downstream claim is consistent with the diff: office365 and zoom call parseRefreshTokenResponse and persist tokenResponse.data, so expiry would be dropped in sync mode and stale expiry would cause repeated re-refreshes. The mechanism is fully veri

judged_text: The computed keys `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (zod schemas do not implement toString for key generation), so the schema collapses to {access_token, "[object Object]"} and, because z.object strips unknown keys, the expiry field the comment says to capture is never kept. In sync mode every refreshed credential is persisted without its expiry (office365-calendar and zoom then see a stale/past expiry on every call and re-hit the sync endpoint each time), and a sync response containing no expiry at all passes validation despite the documented contract.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed object keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These evaluate to a literal string key (e.g. `"[object Object]"`), not a dynamic key pattern, so the schema does not actually accept/retain arbitrary numeric expiry fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in`. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, any real expiry property from the refresh response will be dropped in sync mode, and the second computed key also overwrites the first, so even the intended `z.number()` constraint is lost. This makes the finding’s core claim (schema collapses and expiry isn’t kept / validation becomes too permissive) directly verifiable from the diff.
